note: COMPUTED FROM THE AUTHORS' TRIAL-LEVEL DATA FOR THE TINY ALCHEMY EXPERIMENT ITSELF, not from the Little Alchemy 2 dataset and not from a figure. Source: Brandle, F., Stocks, L. J., Tenenbaum, J. B., Gershman, S. J. & Schulz, E. (2023), 'Empowerment contributes to exploration behaviour in a creative video game', Nature Human Behaviour 7:1481-1489, doi:10.1038/s41562-023-01661-2; file empowermentexploration/resources/playerdata/data/tinyalchemyHumanData.csv from the authors' additional-data archive (48,963 trials, n=97, median 439 trials per participant). THIS IS THE RIGHT DATASET FOR THIS PORT. The paper's headline analysis is Little Alchemy 2 (29,493 players, 720 elements); Tiny Alchemy is a separate, smaller variant run by the same authors, and it is the one this port is named after and modelled on (540 elements, 4 base elements). Using the Little Alchemy 2 figures would have been the wrong game. All three metrics are computed with this port's own definitions: success_rate from the success flag; novelty_rate as a success whose result the participant had not produced before; unique_pair_rate as an unordered (first, second) pair not previously attempted by that participant, matching scoring/score_session.py's is_unique_pair augmentation. Values are the mean across participants of each participant's own rate, with SD across participants. SUPERSEDES every earlier value, and the corrections are large. success_rate 0.40 -> 0.252 and unique_pair_rate 0.95 -> 0.931 were author estimates. novelty_rate 0.35 -> 0.297 -> 0.212: the 0.297 came from Little Alchemy 2's Figure 1c ((50.91 - 4) / 158.06), which is a different game with a much larger element tree, so it overstated the discovery rate for this one by about 40%. Note the players in this dataset take far more trials than this port allows (median 439 against this port's 80-trial, 200-combination cap), so an agent here samples a much earlier part of the discovery curve. Success and novelty both decline as the reachable tree is exhausted, which means these baselines are, if anything, conservative for a short session.
